question: Which of the following is a human-made water body created by blocking the flow of a river or stream?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Reservoir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **reservoir** is a human-made water body created by constructing a dam to block the flow of a river or stream.
 
• Reservoirs are primarily built to store water for purposes such as irrigation, drinking water supply, hydroelectric power generation, and flood control.
 
• Famous examples include the **Bhakra Reservoir** (India) and the **Hoover Dam Reservoir** (USA).
 
• These artificial water bodies help in managing water resources and ensuring water availability during dry periods.
 
• Reservoirs also support aquatic ecosystems and recreational activities like fishing and boating.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lagoon:** A lagoon is a shallow water body separated from a larger water body, such as the sea, by a barrier like a sandbank or coral reef.
 
• **Estuary:** An estuary is a coastal area where freshwater from rivers mixes with saltwater from the ocean, creating a unique brackish environment.
 
• **Oxbow Lake:** This is a naturally formed water body created when a river meander is cut off from the main flow, forming a crescent-shaped lake.
 
• **Dam Construction:** The creation of reservoirs often involves building large dams, such as gravity dams, arch dams, or earthen dams, depending on geological and environmental conditions.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** While reservoirs provide significant benefits, they can also disrupt local ecosystems, displace communities, and affect sediment flow in rivers.
